_note: Curated, plain-language layer over live GitHub data. Edit freely; build.py adds languages, dates and activity. Repos not listed here are not shown. stage = number of steps completed on the track (research: Plan, Initiated, Progressing, Got result, Manuscript written, Submitted, Published; websites, tools and courses: Plan, Initiated, Progressing, Working version, Live).

research.blurb: Questions about living things, answered with data

learning.label: Learning
learning.blurb: Free interactive material for students and researchers

build.label: Websites & tools
build.blurb: Sites and software built for ANGSUMI and its clients

projects.title: GPT Vision meets taxonomy
projects.plain: Can an AI vision model name animal species from photos? A peer-reviewed evaluation for biological image classification.
projects.done: Published in Springer’s Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems (2024), with the benchmark notebook and data.
projects.next: Rerun the benchmark with today’s open and commercial models.
projects.could: A living benchmark comparing AI models with expert identification.

projects.title: Green Heritage of Assam
projects.plain: A meta-analysis of the traditional medicinal plants used in Assam: the seed of the Northeast-wide study.
projects.done: Published in the Journal of Advanced Zoology, with the cleaned dataset and analysis notebook.
projects.next: Extended to all seven northeastern states in the NE India synthesis.
projects.could: An archived dataset with its own DOI for reuse.

projects.title: HydroSink
projects.plain: Do animals' gut microbes get rid of hydrogen the same way? A pre-registered study across vertebrates, using only public DNA data.
projects.done: Data processed, every pre-specified analysis run, manuscript draft v1, archived on Zenodo with a DOI.
projects.next: Post the preprint on bioRxiv and submit to a journal.
projects.could: A reusable pipeline that screens any gene family across public gut metagenomes.

projects.title: NE India ethnomedicine
projects.plain: Which medicinal-plant uses recur across communities that were documented independently, in all seven states of Northeast India?
projects.done: Source-traced dataset, methods specification, data dictionary and a manuscript draft with figures.
projects.next: Finish the manuscript and submit it.
projects.could: An open, searchable database of Northeast Indian ethnomedicine, every record linked to its source.

projects.title: Spider identification
projects.plain: Name a spider from what you can see under a microscope: machine learning ranks 45 species as you answer.
projects.done: Five classifiers compared on 1,721 specimens, explained with SHAP, plus an interactive identification key.
projects.next: Test the models on newly collected specimens they have never seen.
projects.could: A field-guide app for spider identification.

projects.title: Wetland eDNA
projects.plain: Reading which tiny plants and animals live in two Assam wetlands from the DNA they leave in the water.
projects.done: 18S and COI markers processed end to end; raw reads public at NCBI (PRJNA1551452); step-by-step report online.
projects.next: Write up the comparison between the two wetlands.

projects.title: Ant transcriptome
projects.plain: A catalogue of the genes of the ant Diacamma assamense, built from its RNA and screened for natural antimicrobial peptides.
projects.done: Assembly, annotation, expression counts, peptide screening and a completeness (BUSCO) check, with a report.
projects.next: Deposit the assembly and reads in a public archive.
projects.could: A case study and a short research note.

projects.title: RNA-seq profiling
projects.plain: Which genes are switched on in four samples, shown in an interactive report anyone can explore.
projects.done: Quantification, per-sample functional annotation and sample clustering, analysed honestly without replicates.
projects.next: Turn the report layout into a reusable template.
projects.could: A ready-made report template for small RNA-seq projects.

projects.title: Microbiome by season
projects.plain: Profiling bacterial communities with QIIME 2 and comparing their diversity across seasons.
projects.done: Demultiplexing, quality control, diversity and abundance tables.
projects.next: Publish a readable online report, like the wetland project.
projects.could: A worked example for teaching amplicon analysis.

projects.title: PhD: cattle gut microbiome
projects.plain: How living close to people changes the gut microbes and antibiotic-resistance genes of cattle, seen through a One Health lens.
projects.done: Project website with the study design and framework.
projects.next: Add a README, sampling plan and chapter timeline to the repository.
projects.could: A thesis companion site with the data and code behind every chapter.

projects.title: Population dynamics
projects.plain: How do populations grow, crash and recover? Models from a simple formula to virtual animals competing for food.
projects.done: Nine levels and thirty model versions, each runnable in the browser.
projects.next: Formalise the models and compare them against ecological theory.
projects.could: A paper on emergent carrying capacity, plus a classroom kit.

projects.title: Bioinformatics labs
projects.plain: Ten interactive labs that teach real bioinformatics tools with calculators and simulators: no installation needed.
projects.done: Ten labs, from QIIME 2 to AlphaFold, each with working calculators.
projects.next: Add exercises built on real public datasets.
projects.could: A free course with self-check quizzes.

projects.title: ANGSUMI website
projects.plain: The ANGSUMI website: bioinformatics and data analysis for research labs, with free guides and a blog.
projects.done: Service pages, planning guides, blog, structured data and fast, accessible pages.
projects.next: Case-study pages and a new article every two weeks.
projects.could: The main way research labs find and hire ANGSUMI.

projects.title: Academic profile
projects.plain: My research profile and a printable CV.
projects.done: Profile page, full CV and print styles.
projects.could: The first link in every application.

projects.title: Trishul Innovations
projects.plain: A website for a solar and electric-vehicle company, built with React.
projects.done: Responsive site with animations, measured with Lighthouse.
projects.next: Document it as a web case study.
projects.could: Proof of production web work for clients.

projects.title: ANGSUMI blog
projects.plain: Plain, source-cited explanations of analysis choices in RNA-seq and metagenomics.
projects.done: Two in-depth articles, each opening with a short direct answer and linking primary sources.
projects.next: A new article every two weeks.
projects.could: The go-to reference researchers cite when planning an analysis.

projects.title: Brand assets
projects.plain: Social media carousels, banners and brand graphics for ANGSUMI.
projects.done: Thirty carousel drafts and an editorial calendar.
projects.next: Refocus the content on research analysis.

projects.title: Metagenomics toolkit
projects.plain: An easier way to analyse metagenomics data: one command or one window from raw reads to an annotated report.
projects.done: Scope and goals written; home at tools.angsumi.online.
projects.next: Build the first command-line version for 16S amplicon data.
projects.could: An open-source CLI and GUI that labs without a bioinformatician can use.
